Reasoning: isomerisation preserves the molecular formula, so X and Y are two different compounds among the four printed C10H18O entries {2 (borneol), 3 (1,8-cineole), 6 (linalool), 10 (umbellulone skeleton)}; only 1,8-cineole has a plane of symmetry (through the ether oxygen and both bridgeheads, exchanging the two -CH2-CH2- bridges and the gem-dimethyls), so Y = 3; acid-catalysed isomerisation to the cyclic ether 3 requires an O-H and a C=C in X, which only linalool among the remaining candidates has, so X = 6. The explicit atom map from the drawn linalool skeleton to the drawn cineole skeleton is kernel-verified (all bonds preserved, exactly two new sigma bonds: the ether O-C bond and the ring-closing C-C bond).
